item.title: Inflation surges to highest level in nearly two years as energy costs spike
item.summary: Consumer prices in March were up 3.3% from a year ago, the biggest annual increase in nearly two years. Higher gasoline prices tied to the war with Iran accounted for much of the surge.

item.title: Trump says Iran 'doing a very poor job' in reopening the Strait of Hormuz
item.summary: The fragile ceasefire agreement was tested again on Friday after Iran refused to reopen the Strait of Hormuz. Israel and Hezbollah traded strikes in Lebanon, and Kuwait was attacked with drones.

item.title: There's growing disquiet in the military. The Iran war made it worse
item.summary: Since Trump began his second term, his administration's use of the armed forces has left a growing number in the military unsettled, according to NPR interviews with service members and advocates.

item.title: China's Xi meets Taiwan opposition leader ahead of key summit with Trump
item.summary: Xi Jinping and the KMT's Cheng Li-wun agreed to pursue peace, but Taiwan's ruling party worries it will enable Beijing to undermine its democracy.

item.title: Communities are waiting on billions in disaster funding from the Trump administration
item.summary: States say disaster funding from the Federal Emergency Management Agency has slowed to a trickle under the Trump administration. That's delaying projects to protect communities from wildfires and hurricanes.

item.title: Move over, Mr. Ripley. 'I Am Agatha' is a delightfully duplicitous debut
item.summary: Nancy Foley's deviously-plotted novel centers on an aging artist in New Mexico. Brutally dismissive of anyone who disagrees with her, Agatha is a perfectly engaging (if unreliable) narrator.

item.title: In Steven Soderbergh's 'The Christophers,' an aging artist meets his match
item.summary: The newest movie from director Steven Soderbergh, whose films range from Erin Brockovich to Magic Mike and the spy thriller Black Bag, is about artistic legacy itself.

item.title: Stephen Colbert and Marjorie Taylor Greene are OUT. Who is IN? The quiz knows
item.summary: If you keep up with secret identities, you'll get at least one question right this week!

item.title: Women are getting most of the new jobs. What's going on with men?
item.summary: Over the past year, the vast majority of new jobs have gone to women. One economist says to help men find work, we need to embrace ways to "make girly jobs appeal to manly men."

item.title: Overwhelmed by kid clutter? Get organized with these 7 smart tips
item.summary: If your household is starting to look like one giant playroom, it might be time to declutter. Here's how to cut down on stress-inducing mess and decide what to keep, donate or let go.
